events.reason: Weakening urinary stream, nocturia, incomplete emptying

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Roger Desrosiers, 67, for lower urinary tract symptoms. He was evaluated by a urologist in 2017, including a diagnostic cystoscopy that showed an enlarged prostate and no bladder lesion, and has been on tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime since.

Over the past several months his stream has slowly weakened. He gets up at night to void and finishes with the sense that his bladder is not empty. He has had no dysuria, no gross hematuria and no urinary infections.

Other history: Parkinson disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diverticulosis. Medications: carbidopa-levodopa, rasagiline, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, aspirin 81 mg, tamsulosin. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol of note.

Exam: vital signs normal. Abdomen soft and non-distended, bladder not palpable. DRE: prostate symmetrically enlarged, smooth, non-tender, no nodules.

Data: urinalysis negative. Creatinine unchanged from his prior values. PSA 4.3, slightly above the laboratory's standard cutoff but within the expected range for his age and gland size.

Impression: symptomatic BPH with recurrent symptoms on alpha blockade.

Plan: add finasteride 5 mg daily to shrink the gland over the next 6-12 months; continue tamsulosin. Counseled that finasteride lowers PSA by roughly half, so future values should be read with that in mind. Follow-up here in six months with a repeat PSA.

Sincerely,
Urology

events.reason: Painless bright red blood per rectum with clots

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 07/04/2021. Received 07/07/2021.

CC: rectal bleeding.

HPI: 67M with known diverticulosis and BPH (urology visit in January) woke feeling normal, had breakfast, then had sudden urgency and passed a large amount of red blood with small clots. No abdominal pain. No lightheadedness. No fever. Bowel habits unchanged. Never had this before.

PMH: Parkinson disease, HTN, hyperlipidemia, BPH, diverticulosis, occasional constipation.
Meds: carbidopa-levodopa, rasagiline, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, aspirin 81, tamsulosin, finasteride.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol, lives with his wife, independent.

Vitals on arrival: T 36.9, BP 124/76, HR 88, RR 14.
Exam: alert, comfortable. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, not distended, no tenderness, guarding or mass. Rectal: bright red blood in the vault, no mass, no fissure.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, MCV 90, plt 230. PT/INR normal. BMP within normal limits.

ED course: two large-bore IVs, crystalloid. Remained hemodynamically stable. GI consulted, bowel prep started for urgent colonoscopy. Admitted to medicine.

Impression: acute painless hematochezia, presumed diverticular.

Emergency medicine attending

reports.text: Indication: acute hematochezia. Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: rapid purge, fair. Scope advanced to the cecum, identified by the appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve. Fresh blood and clots in the sigmoid colon. Scattered sigmoid diverticula. One sigmoid diverticulum with active oozing at its neck; 4 mL dilute epinephrine injected around it, then bipolar cautery applied with hemostasis. Observed for several minutes without further bleeding. Remaining colon to the cecum without blood after washing; no polyps or masses. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.
reports.conclusion: Bleeding sigmoid diverticulum, treated with epinephrine injection and cautery with hemostasis. Sigmoid diverticulosis. No polyps.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admission 07/04/2021 - Discharge 07/06/2021. Received 07/07/2021.

Admitting diagnosis: hematochezia.
Discharge diagnosis: diverticular hemorrhage, sigmoid colon, treated endoscopically.

Hospital course: 67M with Parkinson disease, HTN, hyperlipidemia, BPH and known diverticulosis admitted from the ED with painless hematochezia. Hemodynamically stable throughout on IV fluids. Colonoscopy the evening of admission, within 12 hours of arrival, found a bleeding sigmoid diverticulum, treated with epinephrine injection and cautery with good hemostasis. No further bleeding after the procedure. No transfusion needed. Aspirin held during admission; resumed at discharge. Diet advanced without issue.

Discharge medications: unchanged home medications, carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID, rasagiline 1 mg qAM, lisinopril 20 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs, finasteride 5 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week with CBC. Return for recurrent bleeding, dizziness or black stools.

Hospital medicine

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit. Discharge summary and colonoscopy report reviewed.

Admitted 7/4-7/6 with painless hematochezia, bleeding sigmoid diverticulum injected and cauterized at colonoscopy. No transfusion. Since home: no further blood, stools brown, formed. Energy a little low the first few days, better now. No dizziness standing up. Back on aspirin.

Exam: BP and HR fine, no orthostatic symptoms. Conjunctivae slightly pale. Abd soft, nontender. Heart RRR.

A/P:
1. Diverticular hemorrhage s/p endoscopic hemostasis - resolved clinically. CBC today. Fiber, fluids. Reviewed warning signs and when to go to the ED.
2. Aspirin - primary prevention only. Discussed; he wants to stay on it given his father's MI. Continue for now.
3. Rest of meds unchanged.

Mr. Desrosiers returns six months after finasteride was added. He notes a stronger stream and fewer nighttime trips. He was admitted earlier this month for a diverticular bleed, now resolved. No hematuria. No sexual side effects he wishes to discuss.

PSA today 2.3, the expected fall on finasteride.

Impression: BPH, improved on combination therapy.
Plan: continue finasteride 5 mg and tamsulosin 0.4 mg. Yearly follow-up with PSA.

Urology

Movement disorders clinic, in-person follow-up.

Mr. Desrosiers is seen for yearly review of Parkinson disease with his wife. He had a diverticular bleed in July treated at colonoscopy and has recovered. Motor symptoms are much as last year. No falls, no hallucinations, no confusion.

Exam: rest tremor right hand, bradykinesia right more than left, cogwheeling at the right wrist. Gait with reduced arm swing on the right; pull test with one step back.

Movement disorders neurologist

- Continue meds. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Question about something Roger is seeing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is his wife writing on his account. For a few weeks now Roger has been telling me he sees small animals running across the living room floor, like mice or a cat. There is nothing there. He isn't upset by it and knows they aren't real once he looks closer. He's otherwise himself. Is this something to worry about? His neurology appointment is April 4.

documents.title: RE: Question about something Roger is seeing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me. Visual hallucinations like this can happen with Parkinson disease and sometimes with its medicines, so neurology is the right place for it. Please keep the April 4 appointment and tell them exactly what you told me. If he becomes confused, frightened, feverish, or the visions change suddenly, call me the same day. I'll send a note to his neurologist ahead of the visit.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Movement disorders clinic

Dear Doctor, thank you for your note ahead of today's visit.

Roger Desrosiers, 68, with Parkinson disease of about five years' duration (also BPH and diverticulosis), returns for evaluation of visual hallucinations. For two months he has been seeing small animals scurrying across the room; when he looks for them, nothing is there. He says nothing about his medicines has changed.

Current medicines: carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily, lisinopril 20 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime.
NKDA. Never smoker; former occasional alcohol, stopped in October.

Vital signs normal.
Exam: rest tremor, bradykinesia and cogwheel rigidity, unchanged in distribution from last fall. MMSE 26/30.

Assessment:
1. Parkinson disease with psychosis (well-formed visual hallucinations).
2. Mild cognitive impairment, MMSE 26/30.

Plan: we discussed the hallucinations with him and his wife. We will see him again in follow-up.

Movement disorders neurologist

Otherwise well. No CP/SOB. No bleeding. Urinary ok.

Exam: BP fine. Alert, conversant, appropriate. Masking, R tremor. Heart RRR. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. PD with psychosis, MCI - per neurology. Added to problem list.
2. HTN, HLD, BPH stable. Continue current meds.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Roger is seeing things again and worse
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is his wife again. For about a month Roger has been seeing the animals in the house again, more than in the spring. Now he is also convinced the neighbors are stealing from him. Nothing is missing. This started a few weeks after neurology added the new pill in October. What should we do?

documents.title: Call to neurology and to patient's wife
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Read wife's message. Called her: no fever, no urinary symptoms, eating and drinking, no falls, no new medicines besides pramipexole since October. He is not aggressive and she feels safe at home.
Called movement disorders clinic, spoke with the nurse; concern for dopamine agonist related psychosis. Their earliest neurologist visit is Jan 9, they will keep him on the cancellation list and the neurologist will review today and call them about any interim change. Wife told to call 911 for any danger to him or others, otherwise call me with changes. Will see their note.
